text.title: Tailwind Patterns with CVA Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules on variant definition with `cva()`, literal class names for the Tailwind scanner, conflict-safe merging with `cn()`/tailwind-merge, compound variants, and defaults. Each is checkable by reading the component file and the merge utility.

rule.statement: A reusable component's class logic MUST live in a single `cva(base, { variants, defaultVariants })` call at module scope, with `export type Props = VariantProps<typeof componentVariants>` feeding the component's prop types. Chains of ternaries in JSX are rejected.
rule.rationale: `VariantProps` derives the prop union from the variant keys, so an unknown value fails at type-check instead of rendering silently unstyled. Ternaries in JSX carry no type relationship to the class strings, so a renamed variant compiles cleanly and produces a component with no intent classes at all.

rule.statement: Class names MUST appear as complete literal strings in source. Interpolation such as `` `text-${intent}-500` `` or `` `p-${size}` `` is rejected; use a lookup object whose values are full class strings.

rationale.source: Tailwind CSS — Dynamic class names / content detection

rule.rationale: The scanner reads source files as plain text and matches complete candidate strings; it does not execute the module. A constructed name is therefore never emitted into the stylesheet. The bug is intermittent, because the class often exists in the build anyway thanks to an unrelated component — so it works in dev and disappears when that other component is deleted.

rule.statement: The merge helper MUST be `cn(...inputs) => twMerge(clsx(inputs))` and the call order MUST be `cn(componentVariants({ ... }), className)` — component classes first, incoming `className` last.
rule.rationale: `twMerge` keeps the last class within each conflict group and drops earlier ones. Reversing the order means the component's own `px-4` is kept and the caller's `px-2` is deleted, so the override appears to do nothing and the caller escalates to `!important` — which then defeats every future override.

rule.statement: Custom utilities, custom scale keys and plugin-generated classes (e.g. `text-display-lg`, `shadow-card`) MUST be registered via `extendTailwindMerge({ extend: { classGroups: ... } })`, and that extended instance MUST be the one `cn()` uses.
rule.rationale: `twMerge` resolves conflicts from a static map of class groups built for the default Tailwind config; it does not read your `tailwind.config` or `@theme` block. An unregistered custom class is classified as non-conflicting, so both `text-display-lg` and the caller's `text-sm` survive in the attribute and the winner is decided by stylesheet order — exactly the drift the utility was added to eliminate.

rule.statement: Combinations that are not the independent product of two axes MUST go in `compoundVariants` (matching on multiple variant keys), never encoded as a fused key such as `variant: "destructive-outline"`.
rule.rationale: Fused keys make the variant set the Cartesian product: adding one size to an N-intent component requires authoring N new keys and updating every call site. Orthogonal axes plus compound overrides keep the additive cost at one entry, and the exception is visible as an exception rather than hidden inside a name.

rule.statement: Every `cva` call MUST declare `defaultVariants` with a value for each variant axis, and the corresponding component props MUST be optional.
rule.rationale: With no default, an omitted prop is `undefined`, cva matches no branch for that axis and emits only the base classes. The component renders — with no size or intent styling — rather than failing, so the regression reaches production as "the button looks wrong on one page" instead of a build error.

rule.statement: Do NOT apply when (a) the codebase has fewer than ~5 reusable, multi-variant components — a single-use component's ternary is cheaper than a variant schema; (b) styling is CSS-in-JS or vanilla-extract, whose own recipe/variant APIs already provide typed variants and scoped class names; (c) Tailwind is not in the build pipeline at all.
rule.rationale: `cva` + `tailwind-merge` buys type-safety and conflict resolution at the cost of indirection. Below the reuse threshold there are no conflicts to resolve, so the abstraction only moves the class strings one file away from where they are read.
